description: Expected results for EPA's official WASP 'Steady State' example (SteadyState.wif from steady-state-example.zip, EPA WASP model examples): a 10-segment river (kinematic-wave flow, upstream boundary + NPDES point source) with 5 systems (Upstream BOD, NPDES BOD, DO, Solids, Temp), 4.96 days, output every 0.014 d. Run with the REAL EPA WASP 8.5.0 engine (waspccli.exe under WINE) through the KI tool tools/run_wasp_engine.py; values read from SteadyState.BMD2 with EPA's BMD2_Extract.exe. EPA ships no reference output for this example, so the values were recorded from our own runs: two clean runs on 2026-10-06 gave byte-identical .OUT, .BMD2 and extracted CSV (deterministic). Segment 1 = 'Downstream' (river outlet), segment 9 = 'PointSource'.
engine_version: EPA WASP 8.5.0 (banner: Wasp suite version 8.5.0, Gui develop af12325 dirty, Model master e86fb43), installer wasp-version-8.5.0-install-64-bit-10-25-2025.exe, under WINE 9.0

recorded_with: tools/run_wasp_engine.py (live KI /mnt/disk1/Hydrocraft_server/models/WASP/knowledge_infrastructure) -> wine C:\WASP8\wasp\bin\waspccli.exe SteadyState.wif; WINEPREFIX /home/server/engine_builds_20261006/wasp/wineprefix; extraction with C:\WASP8\wasp\bin\BMD2_Extract.exe
reference: Own runs (no official EPA reference output exists for this example). Two clean runs were byte-identical.
notes: The run prints 31 'ERROR: Failed to locate time function' lines (the example was saved by WASP 8 in 2017 and is read by 8.5) and the wine exit code is 2, yet the engine closes out normally and writes all outputs. Whether the missing time functions change the science of this example has NOT been checked; these values are a repeat-run baseline for this engine build, not a validated physical result. Water temperature starts from 0 and is still rising at the end of this short run.
